items.english: to look at one's phone
to go to class
to help a friend
two eggs
a watermelon

good for your health

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.pinyin: Bié kàn shǒujī le, xiànzài yǐjīng bā diǎn sìshí le.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: B

title.english: In the kitchen at Wang Ming's home

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 哥哥，你在做什么呢？我来帮助你吧。

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 谢谢你，安娜！我在做鸡蛋面条。
dialogue.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ, Ānnà! Wǒ zài zuò jīdàn miàntiáo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Yào jǐ ge jīdàn?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 四个。你能洗一下这些菜吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Sì ge. Nǐ néng xǐ yíxià zhèxiē cài ma?
dialogue.english: Four. Could you wash these vegetables?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Méi wèntí.
dialogue.english: No problem.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 洗完菜你就别忙了，去休息一下吧。
dialogue.pinyin: Xǐwán cài nǐ jiù bié máng le, qù xiūxi yíxià ba.
dialogue.english: Once the vegetables are washed, stop working and go have a rest.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Méi guānxi, wǒ hěn xǐhuan zuò fàn.
dialogue.english: It's fine, I really like cooking.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, xīguā duōshao qián yì jīn?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Sān kuài yì jīn. Jīntiān de xīguā hěn hǎochī.
dialogue.english: Three kuai a jin. Today's watermelons are really good.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 天气这么热，我每天都想吃西瓜。
dialogue.pinyin: Tiānqì zhème rè, wǒ měi tiān dōu xiǎng chī xīguā.
dialogue.english: It's so hot, I want watermelon every day.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Duō chī shuǐguǒ duì shēntǐ hǎo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 那我要这个大的，再买一些苹果。
dialogue.pinyin: Nà wǒ yào zhège dà de, zài mǎi yìxiē píngguǒ.
dialogue.english: Then I'll take this big one, and some apples too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de, yígòng sìshí kuài.
dialogue.english: Sure, that's forty kuai altogether.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我是马克。我每天早上六点起床，去学校旁边跑步。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ shì Mǎkè. Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang liù diǎn qǐ chuáng, qù xuéxiào pángbiān pǎo bù.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Pǎo bù duì shēntǐ hěn hǎo.
dialogue.english: Running is very good for your health.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 回家以后，我先洗手，再吃两个鸡蛋，喝一杯牛奶。
dialogue.pinyin: Huí jiā yǐhòu, wǒ xiān xǐ shǒu, zài chī liǎng ge jīdàn, hē yì bēi niúnǎi.
dialogue.english: When I get home, I wash my hands first, then eat two eggs and drink a glass of milk.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.pinyin: Wǎnshang wǒ hěn xǐhuan kàn shǒujī.
dialogue.english: In the evening I love looking at my phone.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我妈妈常常在电话里说："别看手机了，早点儿睡觉！"
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ māma chángcháng zài diànhuà li shuō: "Bié kàn shǒujī le, zǎo diǎnr shuì jiào!"
dialogue.english: My mom often says on the phone: "Stop looking at your phone and go to bed early!"

title.english: "不要……了" and "别……了": Telling Someone to Stop

explanation.hanzi: "别"和"不要"放在动词前面，用来叫别人不做某件事。如果这件事正在进行，句末加"了"，意思是"现在停下来"。"别"比"不要"更口语化，语气也比较轻。
explanation.english: 别 (bié) and 不要 (búyào) go before a verb to tell someone not to do something. When the action is already happening, add 了 at the end of the sentence: the meaning becomes "stop doing it now". 别看手机了 is "Stop looking at your phone", not "Never look at your phone". 别 is more colloquial and a little softer than 不要.

examples.hanzi: 别看电视了，我们去跑步吧。
examples.pinyin: Bié kàn diànshì le, wǒmen qù pǎo bù ba.
examples.english: Stop watching TV, let's go for a run.

examples.hanzi: 不要喝咖啡了，喝一杯水吧。
examples.pinyin: Búyào hē kāfēi le, hē yì bēi shuǐ ba.
examples.english: Stop drinking coffee and have a glass of water.

examples.hanzi: 你别忙了，坐下休息一下。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié máng le, zuòxià xiūxi yíxià.
examples.english: Stop rushing around, sit down and rest a bit.

examples.pinyin: Bié shuō le, wǒ yǐjīng zhīdào le.
examples.english: Say no more, I already know.

explanation.hanzi: 介词"对"放在名词或代词前面，说明一个动作或者一种态度是向着谁或什么的。常用格式："A 对 B + 形容词"，比如"跑步对身体好"、"老师对我们很好"。注意：形容词在"对……"的后面。
explanation.english: The preposition 对 (duì) introduces the person or thing that something is directed at, like "to" or "for". A common pattern is "A 对 B + adjective": 跑步对身体好 "Running is good for your health", 老师对我们很好 "The teacher is good to us". Note the word order: the 对 phrase comes before the adjective, never after it.

examples.pinyin: Duō chī shuǐguǒ duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Eating lots of fruit is good for your health.

examples.pinyin: Liú lǎoshī duì wǒmen hěn hǎo.
examples.english: Professor Liu is very good to us.

examples.hanzi: 晚上喝咖啡对身体不好。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang hē kāfēi duì shēntǐ bù hǎo.
examples.english: Drinking coffee in the evening is bad for you.

examples.pinyin: Tā gēge duì wǒ hěn hǎo.
examples.english: His older brother is very kind to me.

singleComponentChars.etymology: The outer strokes are a climbing vine, and the shape hanging in the middle is a round fruit on it. It appears in 西瓜, literally "western melon", because the fruit reached China from the west.

prompt.hanzi: 两人一组，谈谈你们的一天。
prompt.english: In pairs, talk about your daily routines.

activities: Describe your morning like Mark: what time you get up, what you eat, and one thing you do that is good for your health (……对身体很好).

"Annoying roommate": one partner keeps doing something (looking at the phone, watching TV, drinking coffee late at night); the other tells them to stop with 别……了 or 不要……了, and gives a reason using 对……不好.
Phone call: A calls B and asks 你正在做什么呢？ B answers with 我正在……呢, then A offers 我来帮助你吧.
Fruit shop role play: buy watermelon and apples, ask the price per jin, and say why fruit is good for you.

culture.body:
If you walk into a Chinese park at 6:30 in the morning, you will find it already full. Retired people are the early risers: some practise tai chi (太极拳 tàijíquán) in slow, quiet rows, others swing their arms, walk backwards, or stretch against a tree. For many older people, this daily exercise is simply 对身体好 (duì shēntǐ hǎo), good for the body, and the park is free.

As evening falls the music gets louder. Groups of mostly middle-aged women gather in squares and car parks for 广场舞 (guǎngchǎngwǔ), "square dancing": a portable speaker, a leader at the front, and dozens of dancers following the same steps. It is exercise, a social club and a neighbourhood news network all at once, although neighbours who want quiet sometimes complain about the volume.

Parks are also where people sing together, play cards or Chinese chess, write characters on the ground with a big brush dipped in water, or walk a bird in its cage. If you want to practise your Chinese, a park bench in the morning is a great place: older people are often happy to chat with a curious foreigner, and the first question will probably be 你是哪国人？
